adds.title: Gov. DeWine signs bill limiting bathroom use by trans people at Ohio schools, colleges | The Statehouse News Bureau
adds.summary: Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine signed the measure on Nov. 27, 2024; under the new law all K-12 schools and colleges must require students to use bathrooms and locker rooms matching the gender on their birth certificates. The article identifies Senate Bill 104 as the legislative vehicle and notes the bill also designates public and private school bathrooms and other facilities such as locker rooms by sex. For this record: dated confirmation of Ohio's 2024 facility-use law as enacted and signed.

adds.title: Ohio Gov. DeWine signs bill restricting transgender students' use of bathrooms | PBS News
adds.summary: AP report that on Nov. 27, 2024 Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine signed the 'Protect All Students Act,' signing out of public view and over the objections of Democrats, teachers' unions and civil rights groups. The measure requires public and private schools, colleges and universities to designate separate bathrooms, locker rooms and overnight accommodations 'for the exclusive use' of either males or females based on sex assigned at or near birth; it takes effect in 90 days and contains no enforcement mechanism, with sponsor Republican state Sen. Jerry Cirino. Documents the scope (K-12 through college) and 90-day clock of the state's new facility restriction.

adds.title: Ohio Governor Signs 'Bathroom Bill' Into Law, Impacting K-12 Schools and Higher Education Institutions in the State - Ogletree
adds.summary: Law-firm client alert: on Nov. 27, 2024, Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine signed Senate Bill 104, officially the 'Protect All Students Act' but widely coined the 'Bathroom Bill,' which outlines specific guidelines and restrictions for the use of restrooms, locker rooms, changing rooms and shower rooms in Ohio schools, with an effective date of Feb. 25, 2025. Independent legal reading of the statute's facility restriction and its implementation timeline for schools and colleges.

adds.title: Iowa enacts transgender bathroom bill and ban on gender-affirming care for minors
adds.summary: Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds signed two bills on March 22, 2023: Senate File 538 bars doctors from administering gender-affirming care to anyone under 18 (covering puberty blockers, hormone therapy and transition-related surgeries), and Senate File 482 prevents transgender students from entering school bathrooms or changing rooms that correspond with their gender identities. The restroom restriction applies to multiperson restrooms and locker rooms at public and private elementary and secondary schools and took effect immediately, with single-person facilities available to trans students who obtain written consent from legal guardians. Names both statutes behind this record's Iowa summary.

adds.title: Iowa Supreme Court Says Medicaid Must Cover Care for Transgender People | American Civil Liberties Union
adds.summary: On March 8, 2019 the Iowa Supreme Court ruled unanimously in Good v. Iowa Dept. of Human Services that the state discriminated against two transgender women by denying their Medicaid claims for transition-related surgery, holding that excluding Medicaid coverage for gender-affirming surgery violates the Iowa Civil Rights Act. Documents the Iowa court carve-back of the state's surgery-coverage ban for adults that this record references.

adds.title: A Timeline of Litigation for Coverage of Gender-Affirming Transgender Surgery in Iowa - ACLU of Iowa
adds.summary: ACLU of Iowa's litigation timeline for coverage of gender-affirming transgender surgery in the state, from the lawsuit filed on behalf of Mika Covington and Aiden Vasquez over Iowa Medicaid's refusal to cover medically necessary gender-affirming surgery, through the March 2019 Iowa Supreme Court ruling and the litigation that followed. Tracks the state-court path that kept Medicaid surgery coverage available to transgender adults in Iowa.

adds.title: Iowa schools are scrambling to comply with new transgender bathroom law - KTVZ
adds.summary: KCCI (Des Moines) reporting syndicated by KTVZ: Gov. Kim Reynolds signed SF 482 into law on March 22, 2023, requiring anyone in an Iowa school, including students, staff, parents and visitors, to use only restrooms and other changing areas that correspond with the biological sex listed on their birth certificate, and Iowa school districts are scrambling to comply as the restriction takes effect. States the exact statute and subject scope (everyone on school grounds) behind Iowa's public-facility-use law.

adds.title: Governor Pillen Establishes Women's Bill of Rights by Executive Order | Office of Governor Jim Pillen
adds.summary: Governor's office announcement: on Aug. 30, 2023 Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen signed an executive order establishing the Women's Bill of Rights, making him the second U.S. governor to sign such an order 'declaring the biological definition of male and female.' The order backs single-sex spaces for women's sports, bathrooms and changing rooms and states that a person's biological sex is defined at birth. Primary state-government source for Nebraska's sex-definition policy.

adds.title: Nebraska governor signs contentious executive order defining 'male' and 'female' - JURIST - News
adds.summary: Legal-news report: Nebraska Executive Order No. 23-16 signed Aug. 30, 2023 defines the terms sex, female, male, woman, girl, man, boy, mother and father for use by state agencies, stating there are biological differences between males and females in athletic abilities and safety that warrant sex-based segregation for some athletic, social and educational spaces. Reports that opponents questioned the order's scope and legality, and links the order text itself.

adds.title: Nebraska governor signs executive order specifically defining females, males
adds.summary: Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen signed an executive order on Aug. 30, 2023 establishing a Women's Bill of Rights, declaring a 'biological definition of male and female' and detailing the distinctions state agencies must apply. Local Nebraska news confirmation of the signing date and content of the executive order this record is about.

adds.title: Kentucky Legislature overrides Beshear veto and passes anti-transgender law
adds.summary: Louisville Public Media: on March 29, 2023 the Kentucky legislature overrode Gov. Andy Beshear's veto, enacting Senate Bill 150, which bans gender-affirming medical care for transgender minors in Kentucky and restricts which bathrooms those students can use in public schools. Names the single 2023 statute that carries the K-12 school facility restriction this record is about, with the override date and bill number.

adds.title: Kentucky Department of Education releases guidance for districts on implementing anti-LGBTQ rules | WKMS
adds.summary: The Kentucky Department of Education in April 2023 released guidance for school districts implementing the new anti-LGBTQ rules, advising districts to remove sex education from fifth-grade curriculum and to tread cautiously with the bathroom-ban provisions. Confirms the school-side operation of Kentucky's 2023 facility restriction and that K-12 districts were the implementing bodies.

adds.title: Kentucky's ban on gender-affirming care takes effect as federal judge lifts injunction | PBS News
adds.summary: On July 14, 2023, U.S. District Judge David Hale lifted the injunction he had issued the previous month, allowing Kentucky's ban on gender-affirming care for minors to take effect and preventing transgender minors from accessing puberty blockers and hormone therapy. Seven transgender children and their parents had sued to block the law, and the ACLU of Kentucky called the ruling a temporary setback. Dated outcome of federal litigation over the same 2023 statute that contains the school bathroom restriction.

adds.title: North Carolina's transgender bathroom battle: what sparked it, and what's next | North Carolina | The Guardian
adds.summary: Explainer of HB 2's origins: after the Charlotte city council in March 2016 passed an ordinance allowing transgender people to use bathrooms matching their gender identity, the state legislature in emergency session passed House Bill 2, which bars cities from passing anti-discrimination ordinances protecting gay and transgender people. The law drew global backlash with companies including Google and Disney pledging to pull back business, and the U.S. Justice Department called HB 2 'state-sponsored discrimination' and sued, with North Carolina filing its own suit. Names HB 2 as the archetype bathroom bill behind this record.

adds.title: A State Divided: HB2 And Transgender Rights | WUNC News
adds.summary: WUNC's North Carolina series on House Bill 2 states that the law requires people to use public bathrooms that correspond with the sex listed on their birth certificate, and records that on March 30, 2017 legislators in the North Carolina General Assembly passed a measure that repealed House Bill 2. Covers both the birth-certificate-sex bathroom rule and its 2017 repeal by the state legislature, matching this record's HB 2 arc.

adds.title: NC Republicans push new bathroom bill years after boycotts over similar legislation :: WRAL.com
adds.summary: WRAL, March 25, 2025: North Carolina made national news in 2016 for transgender bathroom rules that Republicans later repealed in the face of boycotts, and GOP lawmakers in the 2025 session are again pushing a bathroom bill. Shows the state's facility-use policy remains an active legislative subject years after HB 2, supporting the record's 'archetype of legislative instability' framing.

adds.title: Gov. Larry Rhoden signs anti-trans bathroom bill HB 1259 into law in South Dakota | Argus Leader via Yahoo News
adds.summary: Reports that Gov. Larry Rhoden's office announced on Friday, March 21, 2025 that he signed House Bill 1259 the previous day, restricting trans people from using bathrooms matching their gender identity in public schools and state-owned buildings. The measure takes effect July 1, 2025 and marks the first time in state history that any similar anti-trans bathroom bill has made it onto the books, after similar legislation failed in 2016, 2017, twice in 2018 and in 2022. For this record: primary-outlet confirmation of the signing date, bill number, scope and effective date of South Dakota's 2025 facility ban.

adds.title: A South Dakota Bathroom Bill Could Force Trans Inmates Into Solitary Confinement | Them
adds.summary: Detailed reporting on the vehicle behind South Dakota's 2025 facility restriction: House Bill 1259, which passed the state House by a 49-21 vote and would limit restrooms, locker rooms and changing areas in state-run facilities to the same 'biological sex,' primarily targeting K-12 schools and state colleges including off-campus activities. The article documents how the bill's 'reasonable accommodation' clause and floor debate raised the prospect that incarcerated trans people would be placed in solitary confinement to comply. For this record: bill number, House vote margin and the institutional scope (including prisons) of the law signed in March 2025.

adds.title: Governor signs bathroom bills mandating who can use which facilities | News Letter Journal (Wyoming News Exchange)
adds.summary: Wyoming News Exchange report that on Monday, March 3, 2025, Gov. Mark Gordon signed two facility measures into law: House Bill 72, the 'Protecting privacy in public spaces act,' covering sex-designated restrooms, showers, sleeping quarters and locker rooms at public facilities, and Senate File 62, 'Sex-designated facilities and public schools,' requiring public school children, pre-kindergarten and up plus charter school students, to use restrooms aligned with sex assigned at birth. SF 62 requires districts to provide a 'reasonable accommodation' to any student who does not wish to use a multiple-occupancy restroom or locker room matching the gender at that student's birth. For this record: confirms both of Wyoming's March 2025 facility bans, naming the two statutes, the signing date and each law's scope.

adds.title: Morrisey signs bill defining 'man' and 'woman' into law | WV MetroNews
adds.summary: Local Capitol report that on Wednesday, March 12, 2025, Gov. Patrick Morrisey signed Senate Bill 456, the 'Riley Gaines Act,' which defines a 'woman' as an adult human of the female sex and a 'man' as an adult human of the male sex and aims to preserve women's single-sex spaces, primarily locker rooms, bathrooms, rape crisis centers, dormitories and prisons. The state Senate passed the bill on March 3 and the House of Delegates passed it on March 6, with Morrisey saying at the signing that bathrooms, locker rooms, domestic violence shelters and rape crisis centers 'should be kept private for women only.' For this record: confirms the March 2025 West Virginia facility-restriction statute, its unusually wide facility reach (including corrections and domestic-violence shelters) and the exact signing date.
